[ old review text here ] if you liked Touhou 18/18.5 and their Ability Card/shop system, then you'd certainly love this. It's a full-fledged roguelike bullet hell shmup with a strong selection of items, a solid gameplay loop, and a bright future ahead from Early Access to release. There are still many issues that need to be addressed (performance and visibility, among others) and more content is to come, but LNS is overall very much worth trying if you're looking for a roguelike that scratches the itch, a shmup with unique mechanics, or a mix of both. also there's muscular reimu what more could you ask for

If there's one thing I can say about this game, it'll be that it has a lot of depth to it. Who knew that a simple game loop of avoiding projectiles onscreen can intertwine with so many customizations and resource management? I have yet to explore every item, but with every new one, there is always the hope that it can be The one thing that can help get me through the level. This game is not for the inexperienced. Danmaku-literate people are those who have the technique (the vocabulary, if you will), to decipher the routes of every stage and boss fight. In this respect, this game's vocabulary is rich, and like any classic, it takes training, grit, and talent to enjoy it to the fullest.

I guess this game gets a recommend if you like to challenge your notions on what a normal Touhou game should be, but be warned that as it is, there's a few issues that may or may not be fixed. Huge eye-strain as it is now. And I thought the old version of Sapphire Panlogism and Incarnation Erased From History are rough. I had to nap after every run to rest the eyes. The bullets, the background, the drops and even your own shot will meld into a mess of colours and pixels. And sadly, I think this game would lose its unique characteristics if these issues were fixed, since the acid-trip visuals are part of the charm, I think. Some attacks are not telegraphed well, or have very little lead time. Some barely gives you time to learn the safespots (if any), and I'm playing on Easy. Then there's this one spellcard by the 3rd stage boss which is like "Stay on top of the screen for 1.30 minutes". =_= Difficulty is really high. Easy is like Hard for the official Touhou games. Mostly stemming from the visual issues. I feel like just brute-bombing through half the bosses' attacks, or just burn as many lives as I have in stock. I did 1CC Easy once, only through sheer resource management. The game has a potential to be a cult classic among the more hardcore Touhou gamers. I am interested to see what the final product will look like, and the devs are hard at work in trying to fix the more important bugs, so that's good. EDIT: After many months, I tried again. On Easy. Still can't 1CC, not like the game allows you to. Wished I recorded the gameplay, it is a mess. I still don't understand what is the dev's goals with this game? When even Easy feels like Lunatic at times. When you really don't have the tools needed to clear whatever BS the bosses throw at you. Easily said, this game is not for me, and I'll probably just uninstall it. Maybe Jaimers or Creepy can work this one out when it officially launches, and I'll watch their gameplay of it. I'm just done with this. Also, playing as Reimu, reaching stage 6, and seeing Reimu lash out at Yukari was very cathartic to see, and gave me the closure to just leave this game to the professionals

[h2] [ Edit on 26/05 ] [/h2] Game is getting fixed up. Patches after patches, devs are doing their best to make true on their word. There are still a few big bugs, but a lot has been worked out already. [h2] [ Review at a week after release out of Early Access ] [/h2] As much as I love this game, as great as this game and could be, I cannot recommend in good faith purchasing it, in its current state. I absolutely adore this game. I can yap (and have) for hours about its inspired design, its great music, its detailed and clearly loving pixel-art and character portraits. Gosh even the background are really cool. the Problem isn't there. the Problem, is that it is currently riddled with bugs, typos and incomplete features. I don't know what made Fire Land decide to release it now. It has certainly been... a choice. Simply, I don't think they knew. They didn't know how much they let pass through. They didn't know that a couple playtesters aren't enough, especially in a game with sandbox mechanics such as this one. As with every indie developer's first commercial release, one must be understanding of shortcomings. The game has been playtested that much is clear, but it hasn't been developer tested. At least, way not enough. Simple pairing of items and mechanics can break for no other reason that they're used together, that they weren't tested. They made transformative changes in places, without testing them thoroughly. Yes, testing and debugging is a long, exhausting process. Like I said before, until the game's issues have been fixed, I recommend waiting. If you feel like you REALLY MUST play it, then do. Absolutely do! You will have great fun! But you will also likely encounter a lot of hitches and setbacks. This review will be updated later on, hopefully once my gripes with the current state of the game have been elevated. This game has the potential to be so great, and I dearly want it to be. I believe they can make it, since they've came this far. Lensed Night Sky is a perfectly fine rogue-like with plenty of elements to enjoy from strictly a point of view of gameplay. At the moment it’s a bit buggy and there are fairly sizable performance issues, especially at the end of the game, but the developers have been making constant fixes! Unfortunately, the narrative is why I cannot recommend it. Without going too much into spoiler territory, the game has numerous charming points and amazing moments that are ultimately cheapened and degraded by an excessive amount of edginess, humor at inopportune moments, an incoherent sense of stakes, and highly unsatisfying conclusions. The narrative just doesn’t respect itself, and I walked away with a lingering sense of frustration and dissatisfaction. If you wish to see my full thoughts, and be warned there are spoilers for literally everything, they can be found in this pastebin: https://pastebin.com/VX8t8mnH

A well written game about space, beauty and love. That is not something one would think would be a hook for a touhou roguelike, but it is possibly one of the strongest aspects of the game, which already has pretty great art in all directions, from the cutscenes to sprites to the renders behind the player as they progress through stages and beautiful bullet patterns that will also come and end your run. But this game is also fun, it's really good at being a bullet hell with some leeway for even newcomers to get used to and experience the story to the fullest with its mechanics and systems to make sure getting used to the genre. It's also funny at times, the game made me chuckle a good amount, but also cry a lot due to how the story was handeld and you can experience it well even without proper attachment and knowledge to the series I would say, since I think this game stands on its own, even if I think the game hits harder if you have prior attachments to the characters it has and the series, its still great time. And as a Touhou fan game it also does pretty well in music department itself, jumping from different genres there and there to set the stakes right, remixing stuff from the source material alongside it. Please play it and reach for the stars above, hold onto the memory
